$Comment: Icon intentionally omitted (aligned with the skill-stations-pack tuning leg, 2026-07-22): StationService#blockItemIdAt already falls back to the anchor block's own BlockType id at engage time when Identity.Icon is absent/blank, and this jar's own default Sawmill block shares the SAME id (RPG_Station_Sawmill, filename = item id) - so the summary-HUD crest already shows the station's own block icon with zero duplicated id to drift, the same reasoning the pack's own Sawmill.json/Anvil.json now use. Scope-2 shape migration (2026-07-24, leg A5, jar content re-author to the A-schema): 'Loot.Tables' is renamed 'Loot.Lootables' (the unified LootRef group, asset.LootRef); no other group in this file changed shape (Recipe here authors only FromCrafting, never Conversions, so the Ingredient migration touches nothing here). Every value below is byte-identical to the pre-scope-2 file; only the one key name changed. SELECTION WAVE (decision 56, multi-category picker exemplar): FromCrafting.Categories widened from ['WoodPlanks'] to also include 'DecorativePlanks'/'OrnatePlanks' - genuine native categories confirmed by reading every Wood_<Species>_{Planks,Decorative,Ornate}.json in the shared source (all 11 species share the SAME Wood_<Species>_Trunk ResourceTypeId input and the SAME 'Builders'/StructuralCrafting bench, only the recipe Category differs), so this is zero-hardcoding native-recipe composition, not invented content. The deriver now surfaces 3 output categories per log species (33 total conversions); StationRecipeDeriver stamps each derived Conversion with its source category (decision 56) so the sneak+F picker can offer 'Planks'/'Decorative'/'Ornate' as the three choices for whatever log the player is holding - a single-log input, multiple valid outputs, exactly the picker's reason to exist. Balance-neutral: OutputPerInput stays the reader default (1), matching every derived category's own native OutputQuantity:1. SELECTION WAVE SEAL (decision 57, 2026-07-24): a plain-F press with NO picker selection now defaults to the FIRST AUTHORED FromCrafting.Categories entry - so the array order below (WoodPlanks first) IS the default priority, and plain-F = Planks exactly as it shipped before the multi-category widening (the deriver's alphabetical output-id sort would otherwise have made Decorative the first runnable). Reorder Categories to change the plain-F default; sneak+F still offers all three. This is resolved engine-side at the effective-category point (StationService#effectiveCategory), NOT by touching the sealed deriver sort, so the balance-neutral claim above stays true.
